evidence: Well-defined high-level modules (e.g., history, live, derivatives, symbols, commons) with clear responsibilities
Inter-module dependencies are explicit and direct (e.g., history.py imports from commons, constants, urls)
No process or network boundaries — all modules run in the same Python process
Single package (nsepy) containing all application code, with internal package subdivision (derivatives, debt, etc.) indicating logical modularity
URLFetch and ParseTables in commons are shared utilities used across modules, indicating cohesion within monolith
No evidence of message queues, REST/gRPC APIs, or service discovery typical of microservices or hexagonal architecture
Test suite mirrors module structure (test_*.py per module), consistent with modular monolith testing practices
risks: Tight coupling via cross-module imports may hinder future refactoring or vertical slicing
No explicit boundary enforcement may lead to increasing entropy over time
Scalability limited to vertical scaling only without architectural changes
